sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Bubble Up Endless is a simple yet engrossing game that involves clearing rows and columns of balls of the same color. The game starts with a grid of balls of different colors, and your goal is to create groups of three or more balls of the same color by swapping adjacent balls. However, things get a lot more complicated as the game progresses. The number of balls on the grid increases, and new game mechanics are introduced, such as the ability to swap two balls, remove an entire row or column, or use special boosters to clear the board.

As you progress through the levels, you'll need to think ahead and plan your moves carefully. You'll need to identify the best possible moves to make, taking into account the colors of the balls, their positions on the grid, and the boosters available to you. The game also introduces new types of balls that require specific strategies to clear, such as the frozen ball, which can't be matched or swapped with other balls. The game's core mechanics are simple yet addictive, making it easy to get hooked from the very start.

One of the key features that sets Bubble Up Endless apart from other matching games is its use of boosters. These boosters come in various forms, such as the bomb, rocket, rainbow, and lightning boosters, each with its own unique abilities. The bomb booster, for example, clears a large area of the grid, while the rocket booster removes all balls of a specific color in one go. The rainbow booster, on the other hand, clears all balls of the same color, regardless of their position on the grid. Using these boosters effectively is crucial to progressing through the levels and achieving high scores.
